question: A tree gains 50 kg as it grows. Where does most of that mass come from? Explain.

clusters.label: Believes plant mass mainly comes from the soil
clusters.why_it_matters: Missed by van Helmont's audience 400 years ago and by classes today: if mass 'comes from soil', the whole point of photosynthesis (carbon fixation) never lands.
quotes: Plants get their food from the soil through the roots
Plants eat soil, that is why soil goes down in the pot

reteach.title: Weigh the soil (van Helmont)
steps: Tell van Helmont's experiment: willow gained ~74 kg in 5 years; the soil lost ~57 g.
Ask: if the tree ate the soil, where did 74 kg of soil go?
Land the point: the carbon backbone is built from CO₂ in the air; soil gives water + minerals only.
reteach.check_question: A potted plant doubles in mass but the dry soil barely changes. Where did the new mass come from?

clusters.diagnostic_question: Explain to a younger student why a forest can grow on thin mountain soil without the ground disappearing.

clusters.label: Thinks sunlight itself is converted into plant mass
clusters.why_it_matters: Confuses energy with matter — sunlight powers the process but supplies (essentially) no atoms. This blocks understanding of conservation of mass in reactions.
quotes: Sunlight gives the plant energy and it turns the light into wood
Light energy becomes the plant material as it grows

reteach.title: Energy is not ingredients
steps: Analogy: an oven's heat bakes the cake, but the cake's mass is flour, eggs, sugar. Light = heat; CO₂ + water = ingredients.
Write the photosynthesis equation and count atoms in and out together.
Ask: if light became mass, would a plant in light but sealed from air gain weight?
reteach.check_question: In photosynthesis, which provides the atoms and which provides the energy?

clusters.diagnostic_question: A plant is kept in bright light inside a sealed, CO₂-free chamber. Predict its mass change and justify it with atoms.

clusters.label: Correct: most mass is carbon fixed from CO₂ in the air
clusters.why_it_matters: Core idea secure. Extend toward glucose → cellulose/starch and where the oxygen released comes from (water, not CO₂).
quotes: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide from the air is built into sugars, so most mass is from air
Leaves take in CO2 and make glucose, which becomes cellulose — so mainly air

reteach.title: Follow one carbon atom
steps: Trace a single carbon atom: air → leaf → glucose → cellulose in a trunk.
Stretch question: the O₂ released — which molecule did it come from? (Water.)
Have students write the two-sentence version for a younger student.
reteach.check_question: Write two sentences: where did the carbon in a wooden chair spend the year before the tree was cut?

clusters.diagnostic_question: Where does the oxygen released in photosynthesis come from? Design a test using labelled water.

unsure.why: Too brief to show a belief
Vague — could be soil-group or its own idea; needs your eyes
